# Rome 46 BC – Tools, machines & manufacturing

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Pulleys, block and tackle, treadwheel crane** [`block_and_tackle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/block_and_tackle.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Contractors lift multi-ton blocks with shear-legs, compound tackles and capstans, probably already with the man-trodden great wheel. Caesar's forum and basilica are building sites now. Local: Forum Iulium and Basilica Iulia building sites; building contractors (redemptores).
- **Wheelbarrow** [`wheelbarrow`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wheelbarrow.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Loads go in baskets, on two-man handbarrows or carts. One wheel under a handbarrow frees a man; slave owners see little gain, legionaries digging camps might. Elsewhere: Han China (Sichuan), where it is just appearing.
- **Archimedes' screw (water screw)** [`archimedes_screw`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/archimedes_screw.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Wooden screws turned by treading drain Spanish silver mines and water the Nile delta. Diodorus, writing in Rome, calls it the Egyptian screw and credits Archimedes. Local: Diodorus Siculus. Elsewhere: Spain: mines of the south-east and the Sierra Morena; Egypt: Nile delta irrigation.
- **Gears and gear trains** [`gears_gear_trains`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gears_gear_trains.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Wooden peg-and-lantern gears on water-lifting wheels; fine bronze wheels with hand-filed triangular teeth in Greek astronomical devices. No theory of tooth form, no cutting engine. Elsewhere: Rhodes and Alexandria: instrument makers.
- **Cam and camshaft** [`cam_camshaft`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cam_camshaft.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Cams move the figures of Alexandrian automata (Philo of Byzantium). No cam-lifted hammers or stamps are in use.
- **Screw, nut and bolt** [`screw_nut_bolt`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/screw_nut_bolt.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. The screw is known from the water screw and Greek mechanics. Oil and wine presses still work by lever and windlass, as in Cato. Threads are hand-carved; no bolts.
- **Belt, rope and chain drives** [`belt_drive`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/belt_drive.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Cord drives exist only as the bow and strap that spin drills and lathes. An endless belt between two wheels is new and easy.
- **Ball and roller bearings** [`ball_bearings`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ball_bearings.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Axles and pivots run in greased wood, iron or bronze sockets. Bronze balls can be cast and turned; hardened steel balls cannot.
- **Bellows and the double-acting piston blower** [`bellows_piston_blower`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bellows_piston_blower.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Smiths and founders use paired leather bag bellows worked by a slave. A wooden box bellows with a double-acting piston is unknown and plain carpentry.
- **Water-powered trip hammer and stamp mill** [`trip_hammer_water_powered`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trip_hammer_water_powered.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Needs water wheel and cam, both known in principle. Grain is pounded and ore crushed by hand; fullers tread cloth in tubs.
- **Lost-wax casting** [`lost_wax_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lost_wax_casting.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Greek and Italian founders cast life-size hollow bronzes in sections by indirect lost wax and join them. Founders make statues, fittings and pump parts, not machines. Local: bronze founders supplying statues for Caesar's forum and triumphs; Arcesilaus, sculptor of the Venus Genetrix cult statue (material not recorded), famed for his clay models.
- **Sand and loam moulding for large castings** [`sand_loam_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sand_loam_casting.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Bronze is cast in clay and stone moulds. Iron is never cast: smiths forge spongy blooms, and liquid iron is unknown west of China. No big bells exist. Elsewhere: Han China: blast furnaces and cast iron in moulds.
- **Wire drawing** [`wire_drawing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wire_drawing.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Gold and silver wire is twisted from strip and rolled smooth; iron for mail rings is hammered rod. A hard steel draw plate with tapered holes is new. Local: goldsmiths; mail (lorica hamata) makers for the legions.
- **Rolling and slitting mill** [`rolling_mill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rolling_mill.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Sheet lead, bronze and gold are hammered or cast flat. Small rolls for lead or gold are makeable; true iron rolls in a stiff frame are not.
- **Precision cylinder boring** [`boring_machine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boring_machine.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Pump barrels a few inches wide are cast and then turned or lapped by hand. Wooden pipes are augered. No guided boring bar, and nothing to drive one.
- **Screw-cutting lathe with slide rest** [`lathe_screw_cutting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lathe_screw_cutting.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Turners use bow and strap lathes that spin back and forth, tool held by hand, for wood, ivory, bronze and soft stone. No continuous drive, slide rest or lead screw. Local: turners (tornatores).
- **Precision measurement (flat surfaces, gauges, micrometer)** [`precision_measurement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/precision_measurement.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Bronze foot rules in 12 unciae or 16 digits, compasses, calipers, squares; standard measures are kept on the Capitol. Parts are fitted by trial, not gauged. Local: the Capitol, where standards are kept (the foot is called pes monetalis, after Juno Moneta).
- **Machine tools (planer, shaper, milling machine)** [`machine_tools`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/machine_tools.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Interchangeable parts** [`interchangeable_parts`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interchangeable_parts.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. Army contracts order arms in bulk, sling bullets come from moulds and amphorae in rough standard sizes, but every fitted part is finished by hand.
- **Assembly line and mass production** [`assembly_line`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/assembly_line.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. Large slave workshops (potteries, lamp makers, brickyards) already divide work into steps. No machines and no interchangeable parts; with cheap slaves, owners see little reason.
- **Water-powered sawmill** [`sawmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sawmill.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Timber and marble are sawn by pairs of slaves with frame saws and sand. Needs a water wheel plus crank and connecting rod, neither yet built.
- **Spinning wheel** [`spinning_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spinning_wheel.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. All yarn is spun on spindle and distaff by women of every rank; wool-working is the badge of the virtuous matron. Wheel, cord drive and spindle are carpenter's work.
